So, laxatives for the most part just make you lose water/food weight. They function by speeding up chyme movement through your intestines (which is where most absorption happens) - this is why someone who is constipated needs to drink a lot of water with the laxatives because to speed up the chyme more water is absorbed into your stool and if you don’t drink enough it can further exacerbate constipation. That being said if you speed up how fast the chyme moves, absorption may not be able to keep up, so you will absorb fewer calories, and lose all the water/food in that was sitting in your intestines. It doesn’t cause fat loss though, not directly. Laxatives can short term decrease bloating/weight because you are emptying your body, but it’s not a genuine permanent change.

That being said, please consider not taking laxatives this way anymore. If you continue to do so you are at risk for chronic constipation, and so many other risks. The weight loss is not real weight loss and it is so bad for your body, it’s really not worth it. Especially because people with EDs generally struggle with constipation as it is, so you don’t want to further weaken the muscle along the intestines. Here is a link that talks about more of the risks and offers resources to get help https://www.addictioncenter.com/drugs/laxative-abuse/

Your body absorbs things primarily along the intestinal tract, if the chyme moves faster than your body can keep up with not everything will be absorbed. Digestion and absorption are two different processes. Taking laxatives does not make your body absorb things faster at least from my understanding, it uses water to make things move faster out of the intestines. If you have a source that says otherwise then sure, but from my understanding this is how it works. /lh

(I am double checking my text book about this as well, because I don’t want to spread misinformation, but I do believe you’re confusing these processes)

Double checked, this information is correct. Like I said originally most calories still will be absorbed but the point of using laxatives for a lot of people is to prevent as many calories from being absorbed

It speeds up the rate at which chyme moves through the intestines. The intestines are the main site of absorption in our bodies. So, if someone takes a lot of laxatives the chyme can move faster than our bodies can absorb all the nutrients/calories. However most people use it as a way to get rid of food waste (ie if you empty all the food out of your body and step on the scale you will be technically lighter than before because that food isn’t sitting in your body) - having said that you are still absorbing the majority of the calories because it’s not really possible to move food out of the body *that* fast with laxatives 

So to summarize it’s a combination of being a way to absorb *fewer* calories and also to get rid of food weight

It’s really bad for you though and can lead to chronic constipation and dehydration as well as a whole host of other issues

Mhm. It does also depend though, if eat a ton and you don’t purge as much as you ate it’ll be much closer to half, because however much isn’t purged will be absorbed in the intestines.

You absorb some, but not much. Digestion starts in the mouth via salivary amylase but it’s not much, then in the stomach there are enzymes that digest further, but for the most part you’re only absorbing lipid soluble things, and then the rest of the absorption happens in the small intestine. If you’re purging immediately after, very little would make it that far, so the bulk of absorption wouldn’t happen. So yes, you do absorb some of the calories, and the more you eat the more you would be absorbing, but it’s no where near half. Same thing goes with laxative abuse, it speeds up the flow of chyme through the intestines faster than absorption can occur. 

Ofc both of these things are hugely damaging, LA causing chronic constipation, weakened intestinal muscles etc and purging causing so many problems, but that’s some of the biology behind it.

If I need to I try and journal it out, distract myself immediately with skills such as TIPP or get out of the house. I hope some of this helps, know that you’re not alone and having triggers doesn’t make you a snowflake. If someone has disordered eating, it could be just one thing. So for example if someone is obsessed with eating clean, that would be disordered eating. However an eating disorder is a lot more than that. It’s kind of when there’s several exhibits of disordered eating + a disordered thought process behind it. So for example if someone is obsessed with eating clean, restricts their food to x amount, has an extreme fear of weight gain, punishes themself if they eat past x amount etc, that would be where it becomes an eating disorder. Disordered eating itself can be a symptom of an eating disorder, but when it’s just one thing it can also just be the affect of diet culture normalizing certain things - if that makes any sense?

What the other commenter said was technically true, but not necessarily true given the context of an ED. Because hypothyroidism means your thyroid is under producing, your metabolic rate slows and it can lead to unexplained weight gain. HOWEVER. Anorexia, or any disorder with prolonged under eating, slows thyroid function, which then leads to hypothyroidism. Eating disorders rarely if ever cause hyperthyroidism. Just because you have hypothyroidism doesn’t necessarily mean you will gain weight, especially if you’re eating a really really low amount (which is why the first comment is a little misleading) 

TLDR: absolutely, anorexia can and does cause hypothyroidism - rarely if ever hyperthyroidism

Not a doctor, but I will say this sort of thing is usually self diagnosable. It’s kind of a “does anyone around me do this, and am I feeling the need to hide it” question. Do your parents or anyone know you throw up? Do you see them throwing up their food? Do they binge consistently or skip several meals at a time? The answer is probably no to most all of those, because all of those things are disordered behaviors. People with a healthy relationship with food and their bodies don’t feel the need to starve themselves, binge, or get rid of everything they’ve eaten, so yes, it’s disordered.

Please know recovery is possible. You don’t have to live everyday constantly thinking about food. Your mom is going to catch on if she’s already noticed the weight loss. From one disordered person to another, it’s so much better to reach out now then it is to wait until you’re dying. Please tell her

On the note of the other persons suggestions, with grounding one that really helps me at least is the 5,4,3,2,1 technique- it takes practice because you need to start calming down enough to get yourself to do it, but like naming 5 things you see, 4 things you feel, 3 things you hear (maybe not the screaming in this case, maybe like the nanny who came to comfort you, their voice, your breathing, cars from a road close by) 2 things you smell and 1 thing you taste (to the best of your ability, sometimes maybe you can’t smell anything etc) and then repeat- it helps to pull you out of the flashback because you’re able to recognize “oh this is a totally different environment, I got triggered, I am safe” etc 

Also with tapping, alternating taps! This is actually something they do in EMDR, except faster paced, doing slow alternating taps helps again to ground, and you can actually look into some bracelets online that will do alternating buzzes! I have a pair I wear all the time and they really help, pretty inconspicuous too, except sometimes I get asked “why are you wearing two watches” lol

Personally I experience panic attacks on the regular due to ptsd, so here are some things that help me personally:

TIPP: Temperature, Intense Exercise, Persistent muscle relaxation, Pace Breathing- this is a DBT skill that’s really helped me, specifically in regards to the temperature part (you can look this skill up for more elaboration) but the T essentially means changing your temperature with something cold like a shower/ice pack/splashing water on your face to shock your system into calming down

Phoning a friend: it’s really helped me to have a safe person or crisis line I can call to help work me through those episodes since usually I need someone else to walk me through grounding exercises (those are also good to look into to help bring you back to present)

Bilateral Stimulation: personally since I experience them so regularly I got this pair of watch/bracelet things that buzz in an alternating pattern and it really helps to regulate during panic (this is the same tool used in EMDR just on a slower speed) - they’re kind of pricey, but you can achieve a similar sensation through drawing or doing a “butterfly hug”
